marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q004.takeaway: A hydrocele is fluid within the tunica vaginalis; the source image labels this serous peritoneal-derived sac as layer 2.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q004.displayText:
A hydrocele is fluid within the tunica vaginalis; the source image labels this serous peritoneal-derived sac as layer 2.

The clinical scenario is a hydrocele. It is due to accumulation of fluid in the tunica vaginalis of the testis, which is derived from the peritoneum. When the part of the processus vaginalis between the internal inguinal ring and testis fails to obliterate, it forms a communication between the abdominal cavity and scrotum; this may produce congenital inguinal hernia and congenital hydrocele. The source table describes tunica vaginalis, tunica albuginea, and tunica vasculosa.
emphasis: A hydrocele is fluid within the tunica vaginalis; the source image labels this serous peritoneal-derived sac as layer 2

rationales.a: Layer 1 is not the tunica vaginalis identified in the source diagram; fluid in a hydrocele collects in the serous sac around the testis.
rationales.c: The tunica albuginea is the dense fibrous capsule directly investing the testis, not the hydrocele space.
rationales.d: The tunica vasculosa is the vascular layer beneath the albuginea and is not the tunica vaginalis cavity.

marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q005.takeaway: The genitofemoral nerve's genital branch supplies anterior scrotal skin and its femoral branch supplies the upper anterior thigh.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q005.displayText:
The genitofemoral nerve's genital branch supplies anterior scrotal skin and its femoral branch supplies the upper anterior thigh.

The genitofemoral nerve is likely to be injured. The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve innervates the anterior one-third of the scrotum, and the femoral branch innervates the anteromedial region of the thigh. Clinical note: considering the root values of nerves supplying the scrotum, the spinal block should be given above L1 to anaesthetise it. The source table summarizes scrotal sensory innervation.
emphasis: The genitofemoral nerve's genital branch supplies anterior scrotal skin and its femoral branch supplies the upper anterior thigh

rationales.a: The perineal nerve mainly supplies posterior scrotal/perineal skin, not both the anterior scrotum and anteromedial thigh described.
rationales.b: The posterior cutaneous nerve of the thigh supplies posterior thigh and adjacent perineal skin, not the genital and femoral territories together.
rationales.c: The iliohypogastric nerve supplies lower abdominal wall/suprapubic skin and does not explain the combined scrotal and thigh sensory loss.

The epididymal tail (label C) contains sperm with low-amplitude, high-frequency tail motion in the source comparison.

The tail of the epididymis (marked C) contains sperms with low-amplitude and high-frequency tail movements. Sperm motility is important for fertilization, and sperm acquire motility and maturation in the epididymis. The source contrasts high-amplitude/low-frequency and low-amplitude/high-frequency movements and describes the head, body, and tail of the epididymis. Clinical note: cystic degeneration of the epididymis can result in epididymal cysts.

marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q008.takeaway: The prostate's central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts; BPH most often involves the transition zone and carcinoma the peripheral zone.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q008.displayText:
The prostate's central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts; BPH most often involves the transition zone and carcinoma the peripheral zone.

The central zone of the prostate primarily surrounds the ejaculatory ducts. The source describes three distinct glandular zones: transitional, central, and peripheral. The transitional zone is the most common site for benign prostatic hyperplasia; the central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts and is rarely diseased; the peripheral zone is the most common site for prostatic carcinoma. The source notes that some regard fibromuscular stroma as a zone, but Gray's Anatomy 41e describes three distinct glandular zones.
emphasis: The prostate's central zone surrounds the ejaculatory ducts; BPH most often involves the transition zone and carcinoma the peripheral zone

rationales.a: The fibromuscular stroma is nonglandular tissue anteriorly and does not primarily encircle the ejaculatory ducts.
rationales.b: The transition zone surrounds the proximal prostatic urethra and is the common BPH site, not the ejaculatory-duct zone.
rationales.d: The peripheral zone is the common carcinoma site and lies posterolaterally, rather than surrounding the ejaculatory ducts.

marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q010.takeaway: Seminal vesicles contribute alkaline fructose-rich secretion but do not store sperm; sperm mature and are stored mainly in the epididymis.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q010.displayText:
Seminal vesicles contribute alkaline fructose-rich secretion but do not store sperm; sperm mature and are stored mainly in the epididymis.

Seminal vesicles do not store sperms. Seminal vesicles are paired accessory glandular structures of the male reproductive system located at the base of the prostate. The duct of the seminal vesicle joins with vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct. The mucosa of the seminal vesicle is highly folded and is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium. They secrete white-yellow viscous fluid and contribute to at least two-thirds of the volume of the semen. Secretions are rich in fructose, coagulation proteins, and prostaglandins. They are alkaline

and play an important role in the motility and metabolism of the sperms. The vesiculo-deferential artery, a branch of the umbilical artery is the primary arterial supply of the seminal vesicles. Additional blood supply is from the inferior vesical artery. Venous drainage is by the vesiculo-deferential veins and inferior vesical plexus. Lymphatic drainage is to the internal iliac nodes
emphasis: Seminal vesicles contribute alkaline fructose-rich secretion but do not store sperm; sperm mature and are stored mainly in the epididymis

rationales.a: The seminal vesicle lining is pseudostratified columnar epithelium, so this statement is true.
rationales.b: The seminal vesicle receives arterial supply from branches including the inferior vesical artery, so this is not the false statement.
rationales.d: Seminal-vesicle secretion is alkaline and contributes substantially to semen volume; sperm storage is the false claim.

marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q011.takeaway: The deep (cavernosal) artery gives off helicine arteries that open into corpora cavernosa sinusoids during erection.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q011.displayText:
The deep (cavernosal) artery gives off helicine arteries that open into corpora cavernosa sinusoids during erection.

The deep artery of the penis (cavernosal artery) gives rise to the helicine arteries of the penis. They open into the sinusoidal spaces of the corpora cavernosa. The external pudendal artery supplies the skin of the penis. The internal pudendal artery gives perineal and common penile branches; the common penile artery gives bulbourethral, deep penile, and dorsal penile arteries. The source table specifies their territories.
emphasis: The deep (cavernosal) artery gives off helicine arteries that open into corpora cavernosa sinusoids during erection

rationales.a: The dorsal artery supplies the glans and dorsal tissues but does not give rise to the helicine arteries.
rationales.c: The bulbourethral artery supplies bulbourethral structures and urethra rather than the cavernosal helicine branches.
rationales.d: The perineal artery supplies superficial perineal tissues and is not the origin of helicine arteries.

marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q014.takeaway: Anal carcinoma distal to the dentate line can spread to superficial inguinal nodes; testis, sigmoid colon and prostate usually drain elsewhere.
marrow__ANAT_CH52_Q014.displayText:
Anal carcinoma distal to the dentate line can spread to superficial inguinal nodes; testis, sigmoid colon and prostate usually drain elsewhere.

The most likely primary cause of an enlarged inguinal lymph node is anal cancer. Lymphatics from the anal canal distal to the dentate line (anal margin) drains into the inguinal lymph nodes. Hence, anal cancer arising distal to dentate line can cause enlarged inguinal lymph nodes. Lymphatics proximal to the dentate line (anal canal) drains into internal iliac lymph nodes through superior rectal lymphatics. Option A: In testicular cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the paraaortic lymph nodes. Option C: In sigmoid colon cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the regional lymph node and then to the central lymph node. Option D: In prostate cancer, lymphatic spread occurs to the:

+ Lymph nodes beside the internal iliac vein and in the hollow of the sacrum

+ External iliac lymph nodes.
emphasis: Anal carcinoma distal to the dentate line can spread to superficial inguinal nodes; testis, sigmoid colon and prostate usually drain elsewhere

rationales.a: Testicular tumors spread first to para-aortic nodes along the gonadal vessels, not superficial inguinal nodes unless scrotal skin is involved.
rationales.c: Sigmoid colon lymph drains to inferior mesenteric regional nodes rather than the superficial inguinal basin.
rationales.d: Prostate lymph primarily drains to pelvic nodes, including internal iliac/sacral groups, not superficial inguinal nodes.
